fixes: Stepped side walls: the capstones are separate cubes with gaps between them, so from the 3/4 view (styles.jpg top right, sheet_34 LOD0/LOD1 seed 3) the walls look like crenellations. The sheet-vs-water-2 #2 SIDE view shows a continuous coursed wall that steps down with the treads. Butt the capstones with gaps of 5 mm or less, use capstones 0.30-0.45 m long in running bond across the tread joints, and step the wall top once per tread (kept at 0.20-0.23 m above the tread).

Natural weir lips: with water fx off (styles.jpg natural seed 4, sheet_34 LOD0 seed 1) each lip is one clean, thin, full-width slab spanning between the rock clusters. It reads as a plank bridge, not a rock weir. Build each lip from 2-3 irregular lip stones about 0.10 m thick with 1-2 notches 0.08-0.15 m wide, as in lookbook 04, where 3-4 thin falls cross each weir. Tuck the ends 0.10 m under the flanking bank rocks and keep the crest 0.03-0.05 m below the bank toe.

Natural footing course: every FRONT view on sheet-vs-water-2 #2 shows a pale cut-stone base course, about 0.10-0.15 m high, under the black bank rocks. The natural style has none (verify_sections seed 1). Add a pale stepping_stone ashlar strip, 0.10-0.15 m high and 0.3-0.5 m blocks, along the outer foot of each bank, half buried in kz_ground_profile.

Natural rock shapes and gaps: several bank rocks are still tall pointed prisms. In verify_sections seed 1, the right bank rock rises to a peak about 0.55 m above the bed. Flatten the top facet to at least 40 % of the footprint and cap the height at 0.35 m above water (the r1/r3 target, kept). Close the bank gaps at bends: in styles.jpg seed 4 the ground shows through between the rock clusters. Hold 30-40 % overlap on the outer side of each bend.

Kerbed blocks: at viewing distance the kerbs read as long plain boxes, with faint joints and identical tone. Cut visible V-joints every 0.4-0.6 m (6-8 mm chamfer), vary the tint per block by plus or minus 8 % value, and add a 0.02 m capstone overhang so a shadow line runs along the kerb. Keep the 0.18 x 0.30 m section.

Natural LOD2: sharp triangular fins stick out of the bank strips (sheet_34 LOD2 seed 1, right side; phone-lod2-lod3 LOD2 @15 m silhouette). Replace them with blunt strip ends and keep LOD2 bank heights within 0.05 m of LOD0. Then add the bed cobbles that r1 and r3 asked for (8-12 per pool, 4-8 cm, LOD0 only), which are still not visible.
library_issues: basalt_wet renders warm brown/bronze with bright foil highlights; concept (lookbook 04, sheet-vs-water-2) is near-black wet basalt with gold-lit edges. Darken albedo to ~0.03-0.06 and cool the tint.
stepping_stone treads/bed read well; no issue.
water_river teal preview is a runtime-fx stand-in; not judged.

summary: The from-scratch rebuild is a clear step up. Natural now reads as the arrival-hall rock-lined stream with pools and weirs. Kerbed is a correctly scaled cut-stone rill. Stepped is a real 5-tread, 0.17 m runnel with walls. The remaining weak points are the crenellated stepped walls, plank-like natural weir lips, the missing pale footing course, a few pointed shard rocks, faint kerb joints and fins on natural LOD2. It passes narrowly at 6.0/10.
